purpose: Test whether removing character and bag edges from Canny prevents spatial control from overriding an SDXL identity LoRA.

identity_lora.dataset: 19 approved full-body character reference views only

scene_only_input.meaning: Human-reviewed character-and-bag ROI removed from the Canny map after edge extraction.

comparison.full_canny_0.35_and_0.75: Both scales reproduced the bend toward the ticket and more of the foyer perspective, but changed the white jacket and teal trousers into a teal jacket and white trousers, and replaced the navy flap bag/diagonal strap.
comparison.scene_only_0.35: Preserved the white jacket and teal trousers more often than full Canny, but kept the character upright and replaced the bag.
comparison.scene_only_0.75: Preserved a white-jacket/teal-trouser appearance and camera background, but reduced the character scale and did not create the ticket pose or the diagonal strap.
comparison.conclusion: Removing foreground edges reduces identity-structure interference enough to make scene-only Canny useful for background/camera support. It cannot control the character pose. Canny is not the next pose-control branch; test a separate, foreground-only human pose condition before face or object repair.

retention: The comparison contact sheet, record, and source scripts are retained. The adapter, materialized dataset, and intermediate sheets were removed after review.
